byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: More than a third of Americans were online, and three in ten had a mobile phone.

items.title: Population
items.summary: The United States had about 279 million people in 1999.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Population, total
Our World in Data: Population (UN World Population Prospects, HYDE)

items.title: Life expectancy at birth
items.summary: A baby born in 1999 could expect to live about 76.6 years.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Life expectancy at birth, total (years)
Our World in Data: Life expectancy (UN World Population Prospects and other series)

items.title: Online
items.summary: About 36 percent of Americans used the internet in 1999.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Individuals using the Internet (% of population)

items.title: Mobile phones
items.summary: There were about 31 mobile subscriptions for every 100 people.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Mobile cellular subscriptions (per 100 people)

items.title: Infant deaths
items.summary: About 7 of every 1,000 babies died before their first birthday.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Mortality rate, infant (per 1,000 live births)

items.title: Out of work
items.summary: The unemployment rate fell to 4 percent in December 1999, its lowest since January 1970.

byTheNumbers.scarcityNote: Literacy, household size and vehicle counts were not found for 1999 from a source we opened. There was no census; population figures are mid-year estimates.

clothingAndStyle.title: What people wore
clothingAndStyle.standfirst: Sportswear and cargo pants had gone from the gym and the street into everyday dress.

items.title: Sportswear in public
items.summary: Sportswear became acceptable in public over the mid- to late 1990s, partly through its association with rappers.

items.title: Cargo pants
items.summary: Khaki cargo pants were among hip-hop-influenced sportswear of the mid- to late 1990s.

items.title: A relaxed office
items.summary: By 1996 professional women in America wore more relaxed styles and muted colours.

clothingAndStyle.scarcityNote: The fashion pages we opened date most late-1990s trends only to the mid-to-late decade.

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1999 wage, hours or minimum-wage figures: the earnings table we opened ends in 1995.

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up

items.title: Columbine
items.summary: On 20 April 1999 two students killed 12 students and a teacher at Columbine High School in Littleton, Colorado, the deadliest high-school shooting in the United States at the time.

sensitivity.note: This item describes a school shooting and loss of life.

schoolAndChildhood.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1999 school-year or enrolment figures.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: The last Checker cab retired in New York.

items.title: The last Checker taxi
items.summary: The last Checker taxi was retired in New York City on 26 July 1999 and auctioned for about $135,000.

gettingAround.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1999 fares, journey times or vehicle counts.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: Music files and instant messages moved across the internet.

items.title: Napster
items.summary: Napster launched in June 1999 as a peer-to-peer service for sharing MP3 files, and the record industry sued it in December 1999.

items.title: MSN Messenger
items.summary: The first version of MSN Messenger was released on 22 July 1999.

keepingInTouch.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1999 postage, long-distance or answering-machine figures.

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1999 doctor fees, hospital costs or vaccination figures.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: New cartoons on television, a film in which reality was a program, and a Women's World Cup final decided on penalties.

items.title: New cartoons
items.summary: Family Guy debuted on Fox on 31 January 1999, Futurama on 28 March and SpongeBob SquarePants on Nickelodeon on 1 May.

items.title: The Matrix
items.summary: The Matrix was released on 31 March 1999, followed by Tarzan on 18 June and Toy Story 2 on 24 November.

items.title: The Women's World Cup
items.summary: Brandi Chastain scored the winning penalty kick for the United States in the Women's World Cup on 10 July 1999.

items.title: Dreamcast
items.summary: Sega introduced the Dreamcast console in the United States on 9 September 1999.

items.title: A Yankees sweep
items.summary: The New York Yankees swept the Atlanta Braves to win the World Series on 27 October 1999.

spotlight.title: Y2K and the millennium
spotlight.standfirst: Programs that stored years as two digits might read 2000 as 1900, and by the end of 1999 governments, firms and some households were preparing for it.

items.title: Two digits for the year
items.summary: Many programs stored years as two digits to save memory, so 2000 risked being read as 1900 and machines might fail or give wrong results.

items.title: Preparing the country
items.summary: President Clinton signed the Year 2000 Information and Readiness Disclosure Act on 19 October 1998, and the President's Council on Year 2000 Conversion, headed by John Koskinen, coordinated the federal effort.

items.title: What it cost
items.summary: IDC estimated about $134 billion for Y2K preparation in the United States and another $13 billion for fixes in 2000 and 2001; the page puts the worldwide cost at about $308 billion.

items.title: Stockpiles and cash
items.summary: Some people stockpiled food and water, bought generators and withdrew large sums of cash, and survivalist businesses expected more sales in late 1999, a trend called the Y2K scare.

items.title: A last-minute glitch
items.summary: On 31 December 1999 the Fort Belvoir ground station crashed after a patch, interrupting five spy satellites.

items.title: The rollover
items.summary: On 1 January 2000 few major failures occurred and those reported were minor, such as taxi meters in Singapore and Sweden and 150 slot machines at the Delaware Lottery.
